item.text:
**3B.3 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Working judgment:** `Mostly no direct personal incitement found`. I found repeated evidence of a coercive red-tagging and intimidation environment under Marcos, but not solid 2024 evidence that Marcos personally urged hatred, revenge, dehumanization, or violence against a protected group. The clearest direct quotes I found from Marcos cut the other way.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Against incitement | PBBM declares free, safe environment for journalists under Bagong Pilipinas | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-15 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-declares-free-safe-environment-for-journalists-under-bagong-pilipinas/ | Marcos publicly pledged press freedom and journalist safety. This is the strongest direct statement I found that cuts against inciting hostility toward journalists or civil society. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Against incitement | Philippines not in business of instigating wars, says President Marcos | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-06-23 | https://theprint.in/world/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos/2143467/ | Marcos said the Philippines was not in the business of instigating wars and would settle disputes peacefully. This is a direct restraint statement, not incitement. | 3B.3, 2B.6, 2B.7 |
| Negative / indirect | Philippines: “I turned my fear into courage”: Red-tagging and state violence against young human rights defenders in the Philippines | Amnesty International | 2024-10-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/ | Amnesty says both Duterte and Marcos Jr-era actors weaponized digital tools, misinformation, and anti-terror law to create fear, and that red-tagging by leading political figures and state security actors incited hatred and violence against activists, journalists, and others. This is strong evidence of a hostile environment, though not a direct quote from Marcos himself. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative / indirect | World Report 2024: Philippines | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/philippines | HRW says government officials and supporters continued red-tagging activists, unionists, Indigenous leaders, teachers, students, and journalists under Marcos. It links red-tagging to intimidation and physical risk. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative / indirect | Philippines: Dangerous “Red Tagging” of Labor Leaders | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | HRW reports Marcos-era officials and police or military members repeatedly visited union leaders and threatened them by accusing them of communist links. This is strong evidence of tolerated intimidation, even if not direct personal incitement by Marcos. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative / indirect | Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | The report says red-tagging of journalists persisted under Marcos, alongside libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats. This shows a coercive information environment but does not itself prove Marcos personally incited it. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative / indirect | Philippines: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-net/2024 | Freedom House says the Marcos administration used red-tagging and other tactics to suppress critical speech, while existing blocks on critical sites remained. This supports the inference of tolerated intimidation rather than open personal hate speech. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative / indirect | Philippines: “Red-Tagging” Puts Activists at Risk | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | HRW said red-tagging under Marcos placed leftist activists and critics at serious risk and that officials and supporters used media to accuse them of insurgent ties. Again, this is strong evidence of tolerated hostility, not direct Marcos incitement. | 3B.3, 3B.2 |

**Synthesis**
- I did not find a solid 2024 example of Marcos personally calling for hatred, revenge, dehumanization, or violence against opponents, minorities, migrants, journalists, or religious/ethnic groups.
- The negative evidence is instead structural: red-tagging, intimidation, and coercive pressure by officials, security actors, and aligned media continued under his watch.
- So the best reading is: `no clear personal incitement found`, but `substantial tolerated/incited hostile environment` around critics and journalists.

**Search gap**
- No reliable 2024 source I found shows Marcos himself using explicit genocidal, sectarian, racist, or dehumanizing rhetoric.
- The available record is mostly about state-linked red-tagging and intimidation by others, which is relevant to the lens but stops short of direct personal incitement.
